General Instructions confirm full80 (38 q, 80 marks). Instruction (viii) prints 2 internal choices in B, 2 in C, 2 in D and 3 in E: Q22, Q23, Q28, Q31, Q32, Q33, Q36(ii), Q37(ii), Q38(ii), all found on the paper and each confirmed by a bare OR in the 30/5/3 marking scheme; no other OR in the scheme. Section-A keys read off the scheme pages as images and each re-derived: all agree; no void note. Decimal points are RAISED (Q5, Q34, Q35). Sibling of 30/5/1: 32 rows confirmed on the page and copied byte-for-byte from 2024-30-5-1 (all but Q1-3, Q9-11, Q21, Q26, Q27, Q34, Q35 and the four Q37 rows). Q37 (running passage) is NOT the 30/5/1 passage: this set prints 'mental disorder like depression' where 30/5/1 prints 'disorders' (both checked on the page), so its four rows were transcribed fresh; the table and the parts are otherwise identical. The page render of the Q36 grid figure (idx 18) shows the image tiled three times above a black block, a render artifact; the marking scheme reprints it cleanly (ms idx 14).

| Number of students | 8 | 10 | 13 | 6 | 3 |

Based on the above, answer the following questions :

questions._figure: DECORATIVE - a photograph of a roller coaster; every number is in the passage. Page idx 22.
questions.context:
Essel World is one of India’s largest amusement parks that offers a diverse range of thrilling rides, water attractions and entertainment options for visitors of all ages. The park is known for its iconic “Water Kingdom” section, making it a popular destination for family outings and fun-filled adventure. The ticket charges for the park are ₹ 150 per child and ₹ 250 per adult.

On a day, the cashier of the park found that 300 tickets were sold and an amount of ₹ 55,000 was collected.

Based on the above, answer the following questions :
questions.stem: If the number of children visited be x and the number of adults visited be y, then write the given situation algebraically.
